content:
incident-bot: [ALERT] p95/p99 latency spike detected for streaming endpoints (/v1/stream) in us-west-2. p95 ~ 1.8s -> 3.6s, p99 ~ 4.2s -> 12s. Increase in chunking/missed SSE frames and WebSocket stall reports. Auto-scaling not triggered. Paging on-call. Link: <https://metrics.redwood.internal/d/streaming/streaming-tail?orgId=1&var-region=us-west-2>

sre-oliver: ack, I'm on it. Pulling traces and proxy metrics now.

mia: I'll check the edge proxies and ALB. Noting high `proxy_write_backlog` on stream-proxy group.

eng-ana: seeing a steady climb in origin queue length and socket write latency around 06:13 UTC. Could be slow consumers at the client side causing backpressure.

support-chris: CS reports 3 customers seeing stalled streaming lines and repeated reconnects — AcmeCorp (acct 8462), Shoprise (acct 2233), and an integration partner. Chatted with Acme; they report long gaps between chunks ~6-10s.

ops-lena: quick checks: `kubectl get pods -n streaming -l app=stream-proxy -o wide` shows 8 pods, 3 at 100% CPU, others 60-70%. No recent deploys.

eng-ana: log excerpt from a proxy pod: ```
[2026-03-17T06:12:55Z] WARN write timeout to client (sock=12) after 5000ms, bytes_written=1024
[2026-03-17T06:13:02Z] INFO stalled chunk detected; requeueing request
```

sre-oliver: okay, two hypotheses: 1) client slow-consumers -> backpressure propagates to upstream and causes batching delays; 2) proxy keepalive/timeout config too aggressive causing retransmits.

mia: I spun up one extra proxy pod in the pool to buy time (scale +1). Monitoring if connection stalls drop.

ops-lena: ALB logs show an uptick in `502` and `499` from 06:10-06:18 UTC coincident with the p99 spike. Could be upstream closing connections when write stalls.

eng-ana: suggestion: temporarily relax the proxy's `write_idle_timeout` and increase streaming thread pool for write tasks. Patch suggestion: ```yaml
env:
  STREAM_WRITE_IDLE_MS: 12000
  STREAM_WRITE_THREADS: 32
```

product-jonah: any immediate user-facing mitigations we should turn on? Fallback to non-streaming poll endpoints? Notify customers?

support-chris: CS will send a heads-up to the three impacted accounts with status + ETA. Recommend enabling short polling fallback if app allows; docs link to fallback pattern: <https://docs.redwood.ai/streaming#fallback-patterns>

eng-ana: applying config change to staging now. If staging looks good, will roll to canary subset of proxies (2 pods) and watch p95/p99.

sre-oliver: also adding a temporary rule to evict slow consumers after 20s of stalled writes. Patch command on config-store: `rcs set streaming.evict_slow_consumer_ms 20000` then rollout via config-agent.

incident-bot: action recorded: scaling +1 proxy pod (mia), config change pending (eng-ana), slow-consumer eviction flag set (sre-oliver). Incident severity: SEV3. Paging group notified.

mia: canary patch to 2 pods applied at 06:25 UTC. Early signal: p95 dropped from 3.6s to ~2.1s on the canary subset. Still seeing p99 outliers.

eng-ana: rolling config to remaining proxies now (06:30 UTC). Keepalive increased, eviction enabled.

ops-lena: after full roll, ALB 499s dropped 60% and proxy CPU normalized. p95 now ~1.1s, p99 ~2.8s across region.

support-chris: CS update sent at 06:35 UTC to impacted customers. Acme confirmed improvement and will continue to monitor.

product-jonah: good — can we capture RCA notes for the postmortem? Main causal chain?

sre-oliver: preliminary RCA: workload shift caused a subset of clients to become write-slow (likely network degradation on client side) -> slow consumers propagated backpressure through proxy -> proxy write queues grew and thread contention + keepalive timeouts triggered connection closes -> chunking delays and p99 spikes. Contributing factors: conservative default `STREAM_WRITE_IDLE_MS` and lack of slow-consumer eviction prior to this event.

eng-ana: action items (short): 1) increase default `STREAM_WRITE_IDLE_MS` to 12s, 2) enable slow-consumer eviction by default, 3) add autoscaling rule based on `proxy_write_backlog` metric, 4) add alert to detect rising socket write latency (p95/p99).

ops-lena: I created a follow-up ticket: PLAT-3254 "Streaming proxy: default write idle and slow-consumer eviction" and assigned to eng-ana.

incident-bot: incident status -> mitigated. Monitoring mode enabled for 2 hours.

sre-oliver: handing off to night on-call. If metrics regress, page with SEV2. Handoff note: patch rolled, config persisted, customer contacts logged.

support-chris: thanks everyone — I'll follow up with a brief customer impact summary and copy the incident notes. :thumbsup:

ops-lena: marking this thread for postmortem. Leaving a link to traces and metrics: <https://tracing.redwood.internal/trace/abcd1234>

product-jonah: adding to incident review agenda for tomorrow 09:00.

mia: all good from infra side, reverting manual scale increment now that pod autoscaler caught up.

sre-oliver: last check at 06:57 UTC: p95 1.05s, p99 2.7s. Closing on-call thread.

support-chris: last message to customers sent at 06:58 UTC: "We implemented a mitigation, service is recovering, monitoring ongoing."

incident-bot: thread closed (mitigated -> monitoring).
